title: Early cardiac MRI images identify pleural effusions in retrospective testing
summary: An adapted HRNet segmented early anatomical cardiac MRI images and quantified pleural fluid. In a 200-scan test set containing 42 report-positive effusions, fluid quantification distinguished report-positive scans with an AUC of 0.906. Adaptive scanning and patient benefits were proposed rather than tested.
organization: Imperial College London; Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust

source_review.scope: Read primary full-text cohort, HRNet training, reconstruction/calibration and statistical Methods, pleural-effusion Results and limitations. Author cardiac-MRI page checked; it provides a high-level description, not additional calibration documentation. Supplementary ROC figure not independently inspected. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective 575-scan study across two hospitals and two scanner manufacturers: 375 scans for training/validation and 200 for testing. Clinicians labelled 1,500 development slices. HRNet segmentation and 3D fluid quantification yielded pleural-effusion AUC 0.906 against final clinical reports; 42 of 200 test scans had reported effusions.
evidence.unknown: Report-based reference rather than an independently adjudicated effusion standard; no prospective workflow or patient-benefit test. Generalization beyond these centers remains uncertain. Separate chamber-size claims require manufacturer-specific regression calibration whose fitting partition is unclear, and are not represented here. Threshold-specific accuracy is omitted because optimal cut-offs were evaluated in the study dataset.
evidence.ai_role: An adapted HRNet learned pixel labels from clinician annotations; segmented slices were reconstructed into a 3D fluid volume used to distinguish report-positive pleural effusions.
